name: MedPilot
description: AI receptionist / patient-booking stack for medical practices — after-hours calls, no-show recovery, lead follow-up. Pricing starts ~$297–$2,497/mo (quote-based).

mentions.evidence: ~$44.7k L30, ~$795k all-time, listed MRR ~$302 with 63 active subscriptions (L30 >> MRR — treat as mixed/usage billing, not pure seat SaaS). Founded Oct 2022, US. Last sync Sep 30, 2026. Listed domain medpilothq.com (homepage was unreachable from our fetch; image from TrustMRR landing screenshot).
mentions.indieAngle: Vertical "answer the phone + book the calendar" for one regulated niche beats horizontal AI chat.

whyItPrints: Clinics hate empty chairs and missed calls. High ACV practice software billed on Stripe; L30 revenue dwarfs listed subscription MRR (usage/setup-heavy mix).
whyThisMatters:
A clinic loses the visit when the phone rings after the desk has closed. It loses it again when a booked patient doesn't show. MedPilot is an AI receptionist for medical practices, plus the booking that should follow the call. It covers after-hours calls, follow-up on people who asked and haven't booked, and no-shows.

After hours means the front desk is gone and the phone is still ringing. A lead asked about an appointment and never got one. A no-show had a time and didn't come. Those three jobs are the product. The aim is a chair that doesn't stay empty.

You don't pick a single public price. The quote starts in the hundreds a month and can run into the low thousands. It's billed on Stripe. Usage and setup share the same bill, so a recent 30-day stretch can sit well above the subscription line. The figures are in the revenue block.

The buyer is a clinic. Answer the phone. Put the patient on the calendar. That's the whole job, inside a business that already has rules for how visits get booked.
